newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to lift 2-tier baht system, gives no date.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to lift 2-tier baht system, gives no date.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Wednesday Thailand would lift its two-tier baht system adopted since mid-May to counter market speculative attacks on the currency.
He did not give a date for ending the measure.
"We will lift the measure as it is just temporary. I will consult the central bank governor on the timing," the minister told reporters.
Thailand imposed the two-tier system to cut off offshore baht supply for hedge fund managers who had shorted the baht when they attacked the currency in May.
The move denied speculators Thai currency funds that they needed to fulfill obligations under their forward baht positions.
Currency dealers said large outstanding three-month forward baht contracts are due to expire in mid-August.

After the baht was floated on July 2, analysts said there was no point in keeping the two-tier system. They had expected the government to get rid of the system as part of a series of recovery measures recommended by the Internationl Monetary Fund (IMF).
